questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD skills: multi-container pod design, InitContainers, PVCs, ConfigMaps, Secrets, TLS sidecars, probes, PDBs, and network policies, plus load validation and rollback strategies.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainer for tooling setup
- PVC mounting and data direction between /data/events and /data/enriched
- ConfigMap/Secret for runtime config and credentials
- TLS sidecar for certificate rotation
- Readiness and Liveness probes
- PodDisruptionBudget
- NetworkPolicy for scoped egress
- Load testing and rollback workflow

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: config-aggregator-config
data:
  batchSize: "100"
  enrichmentEndpoint: "http://enrich-controller.analytics.svc.cluster.local:8080/enrich"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: config-aggregator-creds
type: Opaque
data:
  apiToken: <base64-encoded-token>
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: config-aggregator
  namespace: analytics
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: config-aggregator
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: config-aggregator
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: init-tools
          image: alpine:3.17
          command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache curl jq; sleep 0"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /data
      containers:
        - name: worker
          image: myrepo/config-aggregator:latest
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: config-aggregator-config
            - secretRef:
                name: config-aggregator-creds
          volumeMounts:
            - name: events
              mountPath: /data/events
            - name: enriched
              mountPath: /data/enriched
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 9000
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 5
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /readyz
              port: 9000
            initialDelaySeconds: 20
            periodSeconds: 10
      volumes:
        - name: events
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: config-aggregator-events-pvc
        - name: enriched
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: config-aggregator-enriched-pvc
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt this for namespace isolation across multiple environments?
- What scaling considerations arise with batchSize tuning and backpressure?
- How would you observe and debug under intermittent enrichment endpoint failures?

## Why This Is Asked

Assess practical security hardening in CKAD, plus safe rollouts and rollback.

## Key Concepts

- Pod securityContext
- Container securityContext
- runAsNonRoot and runAsUser
- readOnlyRootFilesystem
- capabilities drop
- readinessProbe

## Code Example

```yaml
# Patch excerpt (illustrative)
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 1000
      containers:
      - name: processor
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 9000
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
```

## Why This Is Asked

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal skeleton (Deployment, Secret, ConfigMap placeholders)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: registry-creds
type: Opaque
data:
  username: <base64>
  password: <base64>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: image-scan-config
data:
  registry: my-registry.io
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: image-scan
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: image-scan
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: image-scan
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: installer
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache trivy; mkdir -p /tools"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: images
          mountPath: /images
      containers:
      - name: scanner
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["sh", "-c", "while read img; do trivy image $img --format json >> /reports/scan.json; done < /images/list.txt"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: images
          mountPath: /images
      volumes:
      - name: images
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: images-pvc
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD skills: PVC handling, InitContainers, ConfigMaps/Secrets, simple templating, manifest validation, and network policies. It avoids previous questions by focusing on label injection and re-validation flow.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainer tool installation (kubeval, yamllint)
- ConfigMap/Secret usage for config and credentials
- PVC-mounted manifest discovery and simple file loop
- Lightweight templating to inject labels
- Validation with kubeval/yamllint and conditional POST
- TLS sidecar and readiness/liveness probes
- Namespace-scoped NetworkPolicy restricting egress

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: manifest-tagger
  namespace: <target-namespace>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: manifest-tagger
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: installer
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache kubeval yamllint curl jq && echo done"]
      containers:
      - name: tagger
        image: your-registry/manifest-tagger:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: manifests
          mountPath: /manifests
        - name: tagged
          mountPath: /tagged
        - name: config
          mountPath: /config
        env:
        - name: TAG_KEY
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: tagger-config
              key: tag-key
        - name: API_BASE
          value: http://tagger-portal:8080/api/v1/summary
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
      - name: tls-sidecar
        image: curlimages/curl:7.88.1
        # TLS rotation logic assumed
      volumes:
      - name: manifests
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: manifests-pvc
      - name: tagged
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: config
        configMap:
          name: tagger-config
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the end-to-end flow locally? 
- How would you handle a manifest that fails validation after tagging? 
- How would you scale if the namespace has hundreds of manifests per minute?

```yaml
metadata:
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests CKAD mastery of multi-resource coordination, init containers, volumes, secrets, and network policies. It also validates per-namespace config management and safe log persistence.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob and Job orchestration across a namespace
- InitContainer to install client tooling and share /tools
- ConfigMap and Secret usage for migrations and DB credentials
- PVC-backed /logs for auditability
- NetworkPolicy restricting egress to Postgres
- Status tracking in a namespace ConfigMap

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: db-migrate
spec:
  schedule: "*/12 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          volumes:
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: logs-pvc
          - name: migrations
            configMap:
              name: migrations-config
          - name: tools
            emptyDir: {}
          initContainers:
          - name: installer
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache postgresql-client && mkdir -p /tools && cp /usr/bin/psql /tools/psql"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /tools
          containers:
          - name: migrate
            image: migrate-base:latest
            command: ["/tools/psql","-h","$(DB_HOST)","-U","$(DB_USER)","-d","$(DB_NAME)","-f","/migrations/*.sql"]
            envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: db-credentials
            - configMapRef:
                name: db-config
            volumeMounts:
            - name: migrations
              mountPath: /migrations
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Trade-offs
- InitContainer size vs main image size; tooling duplication
- Per-namespace migrations risk drift vs centralized control
- Secret rotation complexity; ensure timely updates
- Logging volume retention vs cost

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to compose Kubernetes primitives into a practical per-namespace portal while handling content updates and security.

## Key Concepts
- PVC-backed static content
- InitContainer for asset generation
- ConfigMap/Secret usage
- TLS rotation sidecar
- Readiness/Liveness probes
- Namespace NetworkPolicy

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal Deployment skeleton
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: site-portal
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      volumes:
        - name: site
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: site-pvc
      containers:
        - name: nginx
          image: nginx:alpine
          ports:
            - containerPort: 80
          volumeMounts:
            - name: site
              mountPath: /site
      initContainers:
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests CKAD ability to compose a small, namespace-scoped verification workflow that touches ConfigMaps, Secrets, PVCs, and network policy.

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: compliance-api-creds
  namespace: default
data:
  token: <base64>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: secret-allowlist
  namespace: default
data:
  allowed_keys: |
    tls.key
    tls.crt
    creds
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secret-compliance-checker
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: secret-compliance-checker

      initContainers:
        - name: install-tools
          image: alpine:3.18

          path: /healthz
```

## Why This Is Asked

```yaml
# Stable Deployment
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: frontend
  namespace: prod

    app: frontend
    version: stable
spec:
  replicas: 4
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: frontend
      version: stable

      labels:
        app: frontend
        version: stable

        ports:

```
```yaml

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: frontend-canary
  namespace: prod
  labels:
    app: frontend
    version: canary
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: frontend
      version: canary

    metadata:
      labels:
        app: frontend
        version: canary

```
```yaml
# Ingress (production path)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: frontend-ingress
  namespace: prod

    # enable canary routing for the canary backend

spec:
  rules:
  - host: "frontend.example.com"
    http:

      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: frontend-canary
            port:
              number: 80
```

```yaml
# Minimal Deployment skeleton (yaml)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment

spec:
  replicas: 1

      app: flask-app

    metadata:
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical CKAD skills, including permissioning, automation, and Kubernetes-native policy enforcement using a CronJob with ConfigMap-driven behavior.

## Key Concepts
- Namespace-scoped CronJob for periodic enforcement
- ConfigMap-driven policy configuration (imageRepo, imageTag)
- kubectl patch or server-side apply for image updates
- PVC-based logging and HTTP POST for audit trails
- InitContainer for tooling installation (curl, jq)
- Namespace NetworkPolicy scoping for egress control

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: image-tag-enforcer
  namespace: default
spec:
  schedule: "*/5 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: installer
            image: busybox
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl jq"]
          containers:
          - name: enforcer
            image: curlimages/curl:latest
            command: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
            args:
            - |
              # Read policy from ConfigMap
              # Get all Deployments in namespace
              # Compare images against policy
              # Patch mismatched Deployments
              # Write heartbeat log to /logs
              # POST summary to policy-portal
            volumeMounts:
            - name: log-volume
              mountPath: /logs
            readinessProbe:
              exec:
                command: ["test", "-f", "/logs/ready"]
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
            livenessProbe:
              exec:
                command: ["test", "-f", "/logs/alive"]
              initialDelaySeconds: 15
              periodSeconds: 20
          volumes:
          - name: log-volume
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: enforcer-logs
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: restrict-egress
  namespace: default
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: policy-portal
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```

## Trade-offs
- **Frequency**: Running every 5 minutes balances responsiveness vs. resource usage; longer intervals reduce API load but delay remediation
- **PVC vs. Sidecar**: Using a PVC is simpler but requires storage provisioning; a sidecar could stream logs directly
- **Patch vs. Reconcile Controller**: A declarative controller would be more robust but requires custom operator development; CronJob is quicker to implement but imperative
- **InitContainer**: Pre-installing tools increases pod startup time; consider using a custom image with tools baked in instead
- **NetworkPolicy**: Restricting egress improves security but may break legitimate communication; ensure all required endpoints are explicitly allowed
- **Idempotency**: Multiple enforcers running simultaneously could cause conflicts; consider adding a lock mechanism or using `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid`

## Why This Is Asked

## Key Concepts
- Tail -F in a container and in-memory rolling window
- PVC data access and volume mounts
- Writing results to a mounted path
- Lightweight HTTP server for status
- InitContainers, Secrets, TLS sidecar, probes, and NetworkPolicy

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cost-collector
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cost-collector
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: install-tools
        image: alpine:3.19
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache jq curl && sleep 0"]
      containers:
      - name: collector
        image: alpine:3.19
        volumeMounts:
        - name: metrics
          mountPath: /mnt/metrics
        - name: out
          mountPath: /summaries
        command: ["sh", "-c", "tail -F /mnt/metrics/usage.jsonl | ./process-and-serve.sh"]
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
      - name: metrics
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: metrics-pvc
      - name: out
        emptyDir: {}
      # TLS sidecar and service account permissions omitted for brevity
```
